Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) Subject: Proposal for studying and suggesting comprehensive requirement s for the Strategic partnership for CBSE School from K to Class XII through BPCL Foundation. SCOPE OF WORK Engagement of Professional Consulting Agency for Need Assessment, Instit utional Structuring, Project Planning, Regulatory Roadmap, Governance Fra mework and Transaction Advisory for Establishment of a K–12 CBSE School at Chembur, Mumbai 2. Background BPCL Foundation proposes to facilitate the establishment of a high-quality, inclusive, co-educational school offering education from Kindergarten to Class XII, with progressive affiliation to the Central Board of Sec ondary Education (CBSE). The current concept envisages that: i. PARTNER to provide the project land and may undertake responsibility for school operations ii. BPCL Foundation to fund eligible construction, infrastructure, equipment and project-develop ment components through CSR grants received from BPCL, subject to approvals and applicable law iii. BPCL, BPCL Foundation and PARTNER may participate in governance and oversight through a su itably constituted committee or institutional mechanism iv. The final institutional structure, ownership arrangement, management model, funding pattern and contrac tual framework are yet to be determined v. The project requires professional assessment from educational, legal, financial, technical, governance, CS R, regulatory and operational perspective before approval and implementation CBSE’s affiliation framework separately addresses land, physical infrastructure, staff, financial resources, f ees, school management committees, key functionaries, application procedures, inspection, penalties and teacher qualifications. The consultant must therefore treat affiliation as an integrated institutional and infr astructure workstream rather than merely an online application exercise.

3. Objective of the Assignment The objective is to appoint an independent, multidisciplinary professional consulting agency to provide an evidence-based, legally compliant, financially sustainable and implementation-ready framewor k for establishing and operating the proposed school. The selected consultant shall: · establish the social and educational need for the school; · assess project feasibility and optimal scale; · recommend the most suitable legal and institutional structure; · conduct comprehensive due diligence of PARTNER, the land and relevant project arrangements; · define governance, management, control and accountability mechanisms; · develop the CBSE and Maharashtra regulatory roadmap; · review and draft contractual instruments; · prepare the Detailed Project Report; · formulate the construction, funding and operating strategy; · define brand, admission, staffing and school-quality principles; · prepare the complete approval package for the Boards/Trustees and CSR authorities; and · support BPCL/BPCL Foundation through decision-making, negotiation and initial implementation. 4. Guiding Principles The consultant shall ensure that all recommendations: a) advance a genuine public-benefit educational purpose; b) comply with applicable CSR, public trust, education, tax, land, building, labour and child-safety requireme nts; c) protect PARTNER’s title and legitimate landowner interests; d) protect BPCL Foundation’s CSR engagement and fiduciary interests; e) assign clear accountability to the school operator; f) avoid commercialization, capitation, related-party benefit or diversion of charitable assets; g) provide long-term institutional stability and student continuity; h) incorporate transparent procurement, audit and monitoring controls; i) preserve CBSE eligibility throughout the project lifecycle; j) establish an achievable route from K to Class XII; k) clearly distinguish mandatory requirements from desirable quality standards; and l) provide measurable educational and social outcomes. 5. Detailed Scope of Work Part 1: Project Inception and Stakeholder Alignment The consultant shall: a. conduct an inception meeting with BPCL, BPCL Foundation and nominated stakeholders;

b. review available documents, including: i. BPCL Foundation Trust Deed; ii. registration certificates and change reports; iii. available PARTNER constitutional documents; iv. previous concept notes and approval papers; v. land records and proposed site documents; vi. preliminary plans, estimates and correspondence; vii. CSR policies and internal delegations; c. identify factual, legal, technical and financial information gaps; d. prepare a stakeholder map and consultation plan; e. establish the decision points requiring BPCL/Trustee approval; f. submit an inception report, data-request list and detailed work plan. Part 2: Need Assessment and Social Case for CSR engagement The consultant shall establish whether the proposed school responds to a demonstrable educational and s ocial need. 2.1 Demographic and Catchment Assessment The study shall cover an agreed primary and secondary catchment around Chembur and adjoining areas a nd assess: · current and projected population; · child population by relevant age cohort; · current and projected school-going population; · household income and socio-economic profile; · EWS and underserved communities; · migrant and vulnerable population; · employee residential clusters, where relevant; · access to existing CBSE, ICSE, State Board and other schools; · distance, commute time and transport accessibility; · existing school fees and affordability; · enrolment, capacity and waiting-list indicators; · demand for inclusive education and special-needs support; · demand for science, commerce, humanities, sports, arts and vocational pathways. 2.2 Primary Research The consultant may undertake a statistically defensible primary study considering the following - · parent/household survey; · focus-group discussions; · meetings with nearby schools and education experts; · consultations with community representatives;

· consultations with local/state educational authorities where feasible. The bid shall require bidders to propose the sampling methodology and justify sample adequacy. The surv ey instruments must be approved by BPCL before field deployment. 2.3 Supply and Gap Analysis The consultant shall map: · schools within the catchment; · board affiliation; · grades offered; · fee levels; · sanctioned and actual enrolment, where available; · infrastructure and academic positioning; · transport reach; · differentiated positioning; · capacity shortage or surplus; · demand-supply gap over 10 to 15 years. 2.4 School Capacity and Infrastructure Programming Based on demand, regulatory norms and financial sustainability, the consultant shall recommend: · opening configuration and ultimate K–12 configuration; · year-wise grade addition; · number of sections per grade; · students per section; · total design capacity; · classroom requirement; · laboratories, including composite science, physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics, computer, language a nd other required labs; · library and reading facilities; · arts, music, activity and multipurpose spaces; · indoor and outdoor sports requirements; · counselling, wellness and medical rooms; · special education and accessibility facilities; · administrative and staff areas; · assembly, dining/canteen and transport facilities; · security, fire and emergency facilities; · parking and circulation; · staff requirement by designation and year; · indicative built-up area and area statement; · “must-have”, “phase-wise” and “good-to-have” infrastructure.

Part 3: Options Analysis for Entity and Institutional Structure The consultant shall evaluate, at minimum, the following models: 1. school operated directly by PARTNER; 2. school operated by BPCL Foundation, if legally and operationally permissible; 3. school operated by a new public charitable trust, society or eligible not-for-profit entity; 4. school operated through an existing eligible PARTNER educational entity under a dedicated governance fra mework; 5. any other legally permissible and efficient model. The assessment options shall cover: · eligibility under CBSE norms; · conformity with the objects of each trust; · public-trust law implications; · tax registrations and exemptions; · CSR implementation and capital-asset considerations; · land-use structure; · ownership of building and movable assets; · affiliation holder and school manager; · employer of school staff; · receipt and custody of fees; · financial consolidation and audit; · related-party implications; · decision-making rights; · succession and continuity; · exit and reversion; · litigation and enforcement risk; · implementation complexity; · recurring compliance burden; · flexibility for future expansion; · brand and reputation risk. Required recommendation The consultant shall submit: · a comparative options matrix; · advantages and disadvantages; · legal and financial risk rating; · implementation timeline; · recommended structure; · second-best fallback structure;

· conditions precedent to adoption. Part 4: Governance, Management and Control Framework The consultant shall develop a governance framework that distinguishes: · strategic oversight; · fiduciary and CSR oversight; · educational governance; · regulatory responsibility; · day-to-day school management; · financial authority; · asset custody; · escalation and dispute resolution. 4.1 Governance Bodies The consultant shall recommend the constitution and powers of: · trustees/governing body of the operating entity; · School Management Committee required under applicable norms; · Advisory-cum-Governing Committee; · construction/project steering committee; · finance and audit subcommittee; · academic-quality subcommittee; · safeguarding, safety and grievance mechanisms; · procurement or contract committees, where necessary. 4.2 Matters to be Defined For each body, the consultant shall recommend: · number of members; · nomination rights; · independent members; · education experts; · chairperson and member secretary; · tenure and rotation; · eligibility and disqualification; · appointment, resignation and removal; · quorum; · voting; · reserved matters; · casting vote, if any; · conflict-of-interest process;

· attendance and performance review; · meeting frequency; · minutes and record retention; · disclosure requirements; · delegation of authority; · committee reporting; · deadlock resolution. 4.3 Rights and Responsibilities The framework shall clearly define the roles of: · BPCL; · BPCL Foundation; · PARTNER; · any new entity; · landowning entity; · school operating entity; · Principal/Head of School; · project management consultant; · construction contractor; · independent monitoring agency. 4.4 Governance Documentation The consultant shall prepare: · governance charter; · reserved-matters schedule; · delegation-of-authority matrix; · code of conduct; · conflict-of-interest policy; · related-party transaction policy; · whistle-blower mechanism; · document-retention policy; · meeting protocol; · performance-review framework; · draft bye-laws or amendments; · induction framework for committee members. Part 5: Due Diligence of PARTNER, Land and Project Readiness The consultant shall conduct multidisciplinary due diligence and submit red-flag and detailed reports. 5.1 Entity Due Diligence

Review shall include, to the extent applicable: · registration and legal status; · trust deed, constitution, memorandum and rules; · objects and powers; · trustee/managing committee details; · statutory filings and change reports; · registrations under income-tax and other laws; · educational experience and credentials; · litigation, notices and regulatory action; · related-party transactions; · governance record; · authority to provide land and operate the school; · debarment, blacklisting and adverse media checks; · reputation and integrity checks. 5.2 Financial Due Diligence Review at least the previous five completed financial years, including: · audited financial statements; · income and expenditure; · Corpus and Reser · loans and liabilities; · contingent liabilities; · statutory dues; · related-party balances; · grant utilization; · cash flows; · financial sustainability; · existing commitments; · ability to fund and manage recurring operations; · key financial-control weaknesses. 5.3 Land and Property Due Diligence Review shall include: · title documents and chain of title; · property card/record of rights; · survey details and site boundaries; · mutation and revenue records; · city survey plan; · encumbrance and charge search;

· mortgages, leases, licenses and third-party rights; · litigation and acquisition/reservation risk; · development plan zoning and educational use; · access rights; · development potential and planning constraints; · FSI/TDR position; · heritage, coastal, environmental or other restrictions, if applicable; · property-tax status; · Charity Commissioner permissions; · ability to grant long-term, enforceable and uninterrupted use; · compatibility with CBSE land-document requirements. 5.4 Compliance and Capability Due Diligence The consultant shall assess: · track record of existing educational institutions; · academic performance and accreditation; · staffing and HR systems; · child-safety systems; · financial controls; · procurement processes; · technology systems; · complaints and litigation; · capability to scale and operate a premium-quality K–12 school Part 6: Review and Drafting of MOU and Definitive Agreements 6.1 Transaction Principles The consultant shall prepare a term sheet addressing: · purpose and project scope; · contributions of each party; · land commitment and tenure; · conditions precedent; · capital funding; · construction responsibilities; · approvals; · operating responsibility; · governance and reserved matters; · affiliation responsibility; · fees and scholarships;

· BPCL branding; · admission policy; · staff framework; · procurement; · accounts and audit; · performance standards; · reporting; · ownership and use of assets; · insurance; · indemnities; · default; · cure rights; · step-in rights; · termination; · student and staff transition; · asset reversion; · dispute resolution; · force majeure; · change in law. 6.2 Documents to be Prepared or Reviewed The consultant shall prepare or review, as directed: 1. non-binding or partially binding preliminary MOU; 2. long-term collaboration agreement; 3. development-cum-construction agreement; 4. land lease/license/right-to-use instrument; 5. school management and operating agreement; 6. funding/grant agreement; 7. governance charter; 8. asset-ownership and reversion schedule; 9. brand-license or naming agreement; 10. performance-monitoring agreement; 11. confidentiality and data-protection clauses; 12. escrow or controlled-disbursement mechanism, if recommended; 13. amendments to constitutional documents; 14. trustee/board resolutions; 15. required undertakings and affidavits; 16. handover and exit protocol.

6.3 Minimum Contractual Protections The documents shall address: · long-term, binding and registrable commitments; · title and encumbrance warranties; · educational-use covenant; · restriction on alienation; · construction and funding milestones; · utilization certification; · audit and inspection rights; · BPCL Foundation consent for material changes; · change-of-control or change-in-governance restrictions; · performance defaults; · step-in or corrective-action rights; · protection against diversion of premises or assets; · continuity of affiliation; · staff and student protection; · post-termination asset use; · dispute-escalation matrix. Part 7: Educational Model and KPIs The consultant shall facilitate joint discussions and recommend: 7.1 Institutional Statements · educational philosophy; · inclusion and affordability proposition; · positioning within the Mumbai school ecosystem; · graduate profile; · academic and co-curricular model. 7.2 KPI Framework KPIs shall cover at least: · enrolment and grade-wise capacity utilization; · student retention; · attendance; · learning outcomes; · board examination performance; · foundational literacy and numeracy; · teacher qualifications; · teacher retention and absenteeism;

· student-teacher ratio; · professional-development hours; · inclusion and scholarships; · student safety; · complaints and grievance closure; · parent and student satisfaction; · sports, arts and co-curricular participation; · digital and laboratory utilization; · affordability; · operating cost per student; · fee collection and receivables; · budget variance; · CBSE/statutory compliance; · ESG and resource-efficiency indicators; · CSR outcome and impact indicators. For each KPI, the consultant shall prescribe definition, baseline, annual target, data source, reporting frequ ency, responsible owner and escalation trigger. Part 8: CBSE Affiliation and Maharashtra Regulatory Roadmap The consultant shall prepare an up-to-date, stage-wise compliance roadmap covering K to Class XII. 8.1 CBSE Roadmap The consultant shall address: · eligibility of the proposed managing entity; · land and land-document requirements; · recognition and state NOC/DEO requirements; · building and infrastructure; · fire safety; · structural safety; · sanitation, water and health certificates; · laboratories and library; · sports facilities; · accessibility; · staff qualifications; · salaries and service conditions; · School Management Committee; · website and mandatory disclosures; · school records; · application through the applicable CBSE portal;

· inspection and deficiencies; · secondary affiliation; · senior-secondary upgradation; · streams and subject combinations; · annual and continuing compliance. Where relevant, the consultant shall consider whether phased or branch-school architecture is available an d suitable. CBSE’s 2025 branch-school framework allows qualifying affiliated schools in specified circumsta nces to establish a separate K-to-Class V branch, while the main school operates Classes VI to XII, but its a pplicability must be separately verified for this project. 8.2 State and Local Approvals The roadmap shall identify all applicable approvals, including: · educational recognition and permissions; · public trust approvals; · land-use and planning permissions; · building-plan sanction; · commencement and occupation permissions; · fire NOC; · structural-stability certification; · water, sanitation and health approvals; · electricity and lift approvals; · pollution/environmental approvals, if applicable; · traffic and access approvals, if applicable; · food/canteen licenses; · transport permits; · labour and employment registrations; · child-safety and protection requirements; · local-body trade or establishment registrations, if applicable. · Compliance Matrix Part 9: Detailed Project Report, Business Model and Financial Strategy The DPR shall integrate educational demand, institutional structure, infrastructure, phasing, financing and operations. 9.1 Technical and Capacity Plan The DPR shall include: · project concept; · educational offering; · capacity plan; · year-wise enrolment; · grade and section roll-out;

· spatial programme; · preliminary area schedule; · phasing; · high-level implementation programme; · risk and dependency analysis. 9.2 Capital Expenditure Prepare broad order-of-cost estimates for: · enabling works; · civil construction; · MEP; · fire and life safety; · interiors; · furniture and fixtures; · laboratories; · library; · IT and smart classrooms; · sports and playground; · security and surveillance; · accessibility; · landscaping; · project-management consultancy; · design and statutory fees; · pre-opening expenditure; · contingencies; · escalation and taxes. 9.3 Operating Model and Revenue Expenditure Prepare a minimum 10-year financial model covering: · student enrolment; · tuition and other permissible fees; · salaries and benefits; · academic costs; · administration; · utilities; · maintenance; · transport, if applicable; · technology; · insurance;

· scholarships and concessions; · professional development; · affiliation and statutory costs; · lifecycle replacement; · working capital; · operating deficit/surplus. 9.4 Funding Strategy The consultant shall assess: · eligible CSR support during project development; · CSR funding during construction; · funding for furniture and equipment; · pre-operative and capacity-building support; · operating support during ramp-up; · scholarships or targeted student support; · distinction between corpus, capital grant, operational grant and reimbursement; · milestone-based disbursement; · utilization certification; · retention; · matching contribution, if appropriate; · limits and exit from recurring CSR dependence. The recommendation shall identify the conditions precedent to each stage, including satisfactory due dilig ence, land certainty, approvals, design validation and funding sanction. Part 10: CSR Funding Strategy Across the K–12 Lifecycle The consultant shall specifically answer whether CSR funding should commence: 1. from the Kindergarten stage; 2. from commencement of school construction; 3. at the beginning of the CBSE affiliation process; 4. at secondary/senior-secondary upgradation; 5. through a mixed stage-gated approach. Part 11: Branding, Naming and Stakeholder-Benefit Framework The consultant shall recommend a legally compliant branding and recognition framework covering: · proposed school name; · use of “BPCL”, “Bharat Petroleum” and BPCL Foundation identity; · recognition of PARTNER; · logo placement; · campus signage;

· digital and print communication; · annual report recognition; · naming rights and duration; · approval process for publicity; · reputation and crisis-management protocol; · restrictions on unauthorized commercial use; · effect of termination or funding discontinuation. Employee-ward admissions The consultant shall examine whether any preference for BPCL employee wards may be legally permissibl e and consistent with: · public-charitable character; · non-discrimination requirements; · RTE and applicable admission norms; · CBSE requirements; · CSR public-benefit principles; · local/state regulation; · capacity and transparency considerations. The consultant shall recommend a defensible admission framework rather than assume an unrestricted qu ota. Options may include transparent preference at specified entry levels, subject to law, availability and a pproval, without diluting mandatory EWS or public-benefit commitments. Part 12: Construction MOU, Procurement and Independent Monitoring The consultant shall define the contractual and governance framework for construction. 12.1 Construction Responsibilities The framework shall determine responsibility for: · appointing architect and design consultants; · preparing educational brief; · design approvals; · appointing PMC; · procurement/tendering; · contractor appointment; · statutory approvals; · possession and site access; · quality assurance; · programme control; · health, safety and environment; · payment certification; · change control;

· cost control; · delay and liquidated damages; · testing and commissioning; · handover; · defects-liability period; · warranties; · final completion. 12.2 Independent Monitoring The consultant shall recommend an independent monitoring mechanism covering: · monthly physical and financial progress; · milestone certification; · quality audits; · safety audits; · material testing; · site photographs and geotagged evidence; · utilization certificates; · variance and exception reporting; · risk register; · change-order control; · commissioning and handover audit; · CSR-output verification. 12.3 Construction MOU/Agreement The document shall include: · land access; · project scope; · approved budget; · funding caps; · disbursement conditions; · procurement principles; · ownership of work-in-progress; · insurance; · statutory responsibility; · cost overruns; · delay; · abandonment; · force majeure; · defects;

· audit rights; · handover; · title and asset recording; · termination and step-in rights. Part 13: Board, Trustee and CSR Approval Package The consultant shall prepare a complete decision package comprising: 1. executive summary; 2. Board/Trustee agenda note; 3. CSR Committee note; 4. statement of social need; 5. options and recommended structure; 6. due diligence summary; 7. legal-compliance note; 8. land and title summary; 9. financial appraisal; 10. CSR eligibility and funding plan; 11. key risks and mitigations; 12. proposed approval conditions; 13. draft resolutions; 14. delegation of authority; 15. MOU and agreement term sheet; 16. project timeline; 17. presentation for senior management/Board; 18. anticipated FAQs and responses; 19. decision tracker; 20. documents required before release of funds. 6. Deliverable Schedule The bidder may propose an accelerated schedule, but the core assignment should not exceed 12 weeks.

· attendance and performance review; · meeting frequency; · minutes and record retention; · disclosure requirements; · delegation of authority; · committee reporting; · deadlock resolution. 4.3 Rights and Responsibilities The framework shall clearly define the roles of: · BPCL; · BPCL Foundation; · PARTNER; · any new entity; · landowning entity; · school operating entity; · Principal/Head of School; · project management consultant; · construction contractor; · independent monitoring agency. 4.4 Governance Documentation The consultant shall prepare: · governance charter; · reserved-matters schedule; · delegation-of-authority matrix; · code of conduct; · conflict-of-interest policy; · related-party transaction policy; · whistle-blower mechanism; · document-retention policy; · meeting protocol; · performance-review framework; · draft bye-laws or amendments; · induction framework for committee members. Part 5: Due Diligence of PARTNER, Land and Project Readiness The consultant shall conduct multidisciplinary due diligence and submit red-flag and detailed reports. 5.1 Entity Due Diligence

Review shall include, to the extent applicable: · registration and legal status; · trust deed, constitution, memorandum and rules; · objects and powers; · trustee/managing committee details; · statutory filings and change reports; · registrations under income-tax and other laws; · educational experience and credentials; · litigation, notices and regulatory action; · related-party transactions; · governance record; · authority to provide land and operate the school; · debarment, blacklisting and adverse media checks; · reputation and integrity checks. 5.2 Financial Due Diligence Review at least the previous five completed financial years, including: · audited financial statements; · income and expenditure; · Corpus and Reser · loans and liabilities; · contingent liabilities; · statutory dues; · related-party balances; · grant utilization; · cash flows; · financial sustainability; · existing commitments; · ability to fund and manage recurring operations; · key financial-control weaknesses. 5.3 Land and Property Due Diligence Review shall include: · title documents and chain of title; · property card/record of rights; · survey details and site boundaries; · mutation and revenue records; · city survey plan; · encumbrance and charge search;

· mortgages, leases, licenses and third-party rights; · litigation and acquisition/reservation risk; · development plan zoning and educational use; · access rights; · development potential and planning constraints; · FSI/TDR position; · heritage, coastal, environmental or other restrictions, if applicable; · property-tax status; · Charity Commissioner permissions; · ability to grant long-term, enforceable and uninterrupted use; · compatibility with CBSE land-document requirements. 5.4 Compliance and Capability Due Diligence The consultant shall assess: · track record of existing educational institutions; · academic performance and accreditation; · staffing and HR systems; · child-safety systems; · financial controls; · procurement processes; · technology systems; · complaints and litigation; · capability to scale and operate a premium-quality K–12 school Part 6: Review and Drafting of MOU and Definitive Agreements 6.1 Transaction Principles The consultant shall prepare a term sheet addressing: · purpose and project scope; · contributions of each party; · land commitment and tenure; · conditions precedent; · capital funding; · construction responsibilities; · approvals; · operating responsibility; · governance and reserved matters; · affiliation responsibility; · fees and scholarships;

· BPCL branding; · admission policy; · staff framework; · procurement; · accounts and audit; · performance standards; · reporting; · ownership and use of assets; · insurance; · indemnities; · default; · cure rights; · step-in rights; · termination; · student and staff transition; · asset reversion; · dispute resolution; · force majeure; · change in law. 6.2 Documents to be Prepared or Reviewed The consultant shall prepare or review, as directed: 1. non-binding or partially binding preliminary MOU; 2. long-term collaboration agreement; 3. development-cum-construction agreement; 4. land lease/license/right-to-use instrument; 5. school management and operating agreement; 6. funding/grant agreement; 7. governance charter; 8. asset-ownership and reversion schedule; 9. brand-license or naming agreement; 10. performance-monitoring agreement; 11. confidentiality and data-protection clauses; 12. escrow or controlled-disbursement mechanism, if recommended; 13. amendments to constitutional documents; 14. trustee/board resolutions; 15. required undertakings and affidavits; 16. handover and exit protocol.

6.3 Minimum Contractual Protections The documents shall address: · long-term, binding and registrable commitments; · title and encumbrance warranties; · educational-use covenant; · restriction on alienation; · construction and funding milestones; · utilization certification; · audit and inspection rights; · BPCL Foundation consent for material changes; · change-of-control or change-in-governance restrictions; · performance defaults; · step-in or corrective-action rights; · protection against diversion of premises or assets; · continuity of affiliation; · staff and student protection; · post-termination asset use; · dispute-escalation matrix. Part 7: Educational Model and KPIs The consultant shall facilitate joint discussions and recommend: 7.1 Institutional Statements · educational philosophy; · inclusion and affordability proposition; · positioning within the Mumbai school ecosystem; · graduate profile; · academic and co-curricular model. 7.2 KPI Framework KPIs shall cover at least: · enrolment and grade-wise capacity utilization; · student retention; · attendance; · learning outcomes; · board examination performance; · foundational literacy and numeracy; · teacher qualifications; · teacher retention and absenteeism;

· student-teacher ratio; · professional-development hours; · inclusion and scholarships; · student safety; · complaints and grievance closure; · parent and student satisfaction; · sports, arts and co-curricular participation; · digital and laboratory utilization; · affordability; · operating cost per student; · fee collection and receivables; · budget variance; · CBSE/statutory compliance; · ESG and resource-efficiency indicators; · CSR outcome and impact indicators. For each KPI, the consultant shall prescribe definition, baseline, annual target, data source, reporting frequ ency, responsible owner and escalation trigger. Part 8: CBSE Affiliation and Maharashtra Regulatory Roadmap The consultant shall prepare an up-to-date, stage-wise compliance roadmap covering K to Class XII. 8.1 CBSE Roadmap The consultant shall address: · eligibility of the proposed managing entity; · land and land-document requirements; · recognition and state NOC/DEO requirements; · building and infrastructure; · fire safety; · structural safety; · sanitation, water and health certificates; · laboratories and library; · sports facilities; · accessibility; · staff qualifications; · salaries and service conditions; · School Management Committee; · website and mandatory disclosures; · school records; · application through the applicable CBSE portal;

· inspection and deficiencies; · secondary affiliation; · senior-secondary upgradation; · streams and subject combinations; · annual and continuing compliance. Where relevant, the consultant shall consider whether phased or branch-school architecture is available an d suitable. CBSE’s 2025 branch-school framework allows qualifying affiliated schools in specified circumsta nces to establish a separate K-to-Class V branch, while the main school operates Classes VI to XII, but its a pplicability must be separately verified for this project. 8.2 State and Local Approvals The roadmap shall identify all applicable approvals, including: · educational recognition and permissions; · public trust approvals; · land-use and planning permissions; · building-plan sanction; · commencement and occupation permissions; · fire NOC; · structural-stability certification; · water, sanitation and health approvals; · electricity and lift approvals; · pollution/environmental approvals, if applicable; · traffic and access approvals, if applicable; · food/canteen licenses; · transport permits; · labour and employment registrations; · child-safety and protection requirements; · local-body trade or establishment registrations, if applicable. · Compliance Matrix Part 9: Detailed Project Report, Business Model and Financial Strategy The DPR shall integrate educational demand, institutional structure, infrastructure, phasing, financing and operations. 9.1 Technical and Capacity Plan The DPR shall include: · project concept; · educational offering; · capacity plan; · year-wise enrolment; · grade and section roll-out;

· spatial programme; · preliminary area schedule; · phasing; · high-level implementation programme; · risk and dependency analysis. 9.2 Capital Expenditure Prepare broad order-of-cost estimates for: · enabling works; · civil construction; · MEP; · fire and life safety; · interiors; · furniture and fixtures; · laboratories; · library; · IT and smart classrooms; · sports and playground; · security and surveillance; · accessibility; · landscaping; · project-management consultancy; · design and statutory fees; · pre-opening expenditure; · contingencies; · escalation and taxes. 9.3 Operating Model and Revenue Expenditure Prepare a minimum 10-year financial model covering: · student enrolment; · tuition and other permissible fees; · salaries and benefits; · academic costs; · administration; · utilities; · maintenance; · transport, if applicable; · technology; · insurance;

· scholarships and concessions; · professional development; · affiliation and statutory costs; · lifecycle replacement; · working capital; · operating deficit/surplus. 9.4 Funding Strategy The consultant shall assess: · eligible CSR support during project development; · CSR funding during construction; · funding for furniture and equipment; · pre-operative and capacity-building support; · operating support during ramp-up; · scholarships or targeted student support; · distinction between corpus, capital grant, operational grant and reimbursement; · milestone-based disbursement; · utilization certification; · retention; · matching contribution, if appropriate; · limits and exit from recurring CSR dependence. The recommendation shall identify the conditions precedent to each stage, including satisfactory due dilig ence, land certainty, approvals, design validation and funding sanction. Part 10: CSR Funding Strategy Across the K–12 Lifecycle The consultant shall specifically answer whether CSR funding should commence: 1. from the Kindergarten stage; 2. from commencement of school construction; 3. at the beginning of the CBSE affiliation process; 4. at secondary/senior-secondary upgradation; 5. through a mixed stage-gated approach. Part 11: Branding, Naming and Stakeholder-Benefit Framework The consultant shall recommend a legally compliant branding and recognition framework covering: · proposed school name; · use of “BPCL”, “Bharat Petroleum” and BPCL Foundation identity; · recognition of PARTNER; · logo placement; · campus signage;

· digital and print communication; · annual report recognition; · naming rights and duration; · approval process for publicity; · reputation and crisis-management protocol; · restrictions on unauthorized commercial use; · effect of termination or funding discontinuation. Employee-ward admissions The consultant shall examine whether any preference for BPCL employee wards may be legally permissibl e and consistent with: · public-charitable character; · non-discrimination requirements; · RTE and applicable admission norms; · CBSE requirements; · CSR public-benefit principles; · local/state regulation; · capacity and transparency considerations. The consultant shall recommend a defensible admission framework rather than assume an unrestricted qu ota. Options may include transparent preference at specified entry levels, subject to law, availability and a pproval, without diluting mandatory EWS or public-benefit commitments. Part 12: Construction MOU, Procurement and Independent Monitoring The consultant shall define the contractual and governance framework for construction. 12.1 Construction Responsibilities The framework shall determine responsibility for: · appointing architect and design consultants; · preparing educational brief; · design approvals; · appointing PMC; · procurement/tendering; · contractor appointment; · statutory approvals; · possession and site access; · quality assurance; · programme control; · health, safety and environment; · payment certification; · change control;

· cost control; · delay and liquidated damages; · testing and commissioning; · handover; · defects-liability period; · warranties; · final completion. 12.2 Independent Monitoring The consultant shall recommend an independent monitoring mechanism covering: · monthly physical and financial progress; · milestone certification; · quality audits; · safety audits; · material testing; · site photographs and geotagged evidence; · utilization certificates; · variance and exception reporting; · risk register; · change-order control; · commissioning and handover audit; · CSR-output verification. 12.3 Construction MOU/Agreement The document shall include: · land access; · project scope; · approved budget; · funding caps; · disbursement conditions; · procurement principles; · ownership of work-in-progress; · insurance; · statutory responsibility; · cost overruns; · delay; · abandonment; · force majeure; · defects;

· audit rights; · handover; · title and asset recording; · termination and step-in rights.
